comparison: Both strongly support the main conclusion that NTD and CTD do not bind at rest (C5, C6, C97, C110, C111). OpenEval cites convergent evidence from ACCuRET, MST, and overall patterns. Peer reviewers unanimously affirm this finding as compelling, with all three reviewers and the editor explicitly endorsing the evidence against the prior binding hypothesis.

Perfect agreement on MST data (C89, C90). Both OpenEval and peer review (Reviewer 3) support the finding that isolated NTD and CTD peptides show no binding interaction. OpenEval notes the limitation that isolated peptides may not fully recapitulate full-length behavior, but this doesn't undermine the main conclusion.

Both support the functional characterization data (C63-C69). OpenEval emphasizes that L-ANAP incorporation doesn't disrupt channel gating, which is critical for interpreting structural measurements. Peer Reviewer 1 states techniques are appropriate and results are clear and high quality. Complete agreement on this validation.

Both support the pH-insensitivity controls for L-ANAP (C71-C75). OpenEval emphasizes this as a critical control demonstrating measured FRET changes reflect conformational changes rather than probe pH sensitivity. Peer Reviewer 2 praises these as good controls. Complete agreement on this methodological validation.

Both support NTD membrane topology findings (C91, C92, C116). OpenEval finds memFRET data shows parallel membrane orientation at pH 8. Peer Reviewer 3 explicitly states NTD is parallel to membrane and moves toward it upon acidification. Agreement on NTD positioning and consistency with prior work (Couch et al., 2021).

Both support ACCuRET distance measurements (C78-C82) showing ~20-23 Å NTD-CTD distances. OpenEval emphasizes these distances contradict prior binding hypothesis. Peer reviewers find distance measurements coherent and favor interpretation that termini are not close together. Strong agreement on this key evidence.

Both support Zn2+ negative controls (C84-C86). OpenEval notes these validate metal-dependent quenching in ACCuRET experiments. Peer Reviewer 2 explicitly praises the controls as good. Complete agreement on this methodological validation.

Divergence on CTD movement interpretation (C87, C88). OpenEval supports the finding that distal CTD positions show larger pH-dependent movements, suggesting complex conformational rearrangements. Peer Reviewer 3 identifies an apparent inconsistency: unclear how NTD moves closer to membrane and CTD while CTD moves away from membrane. Peer review finds this data difficult to reconcile.

Related to CTD membrane proximity (C93-C95). OpenEval supports the surprising finding that CTD adopts membrane-proximal conformation at pH 8 and moves away during acidification. Peer Reviewer 3's concern about inconsistent movement patterns (R4) relates to reconciling this CTD behavior with other findings.

Both rate the alternative hypothesis (C159, C163, C164) similarly but differently. OpenEval marks as UNCERTAIN, noting the membrane-proximity hypothesis is consistent with data but speculative and untested. Peer reviewers mark as SUPPORTED, with editor noting it provides 'fresh perspective' and Reviewer 1 acknowledging the hypothesis without criticism. Peer review more accepting of the speculative model.

Divergence on amber suppression validation (C57-C62). OpenEval supports the method with appropriate controls, noting Western blots and fluorescence show full-length channels only with L-ANAP present. Peer Reviewer 1 raises concerns about apparent read-through in several constructs and potential co-assembly of truncated subunits, marking as UNCERTAIN. Significant disagreement on methodological validity.

Divergence on unroofing method validation (C76, C77, C133-C136). OpenEval supports the method, noting colocalization validates preservation of channel integrity. Peer Reviewers 2 and 3 mark as UNCERTAIN, concerned that unroofing disrupts cytoplasm and could disrupt interactions, and that pH changes affect both membrane leaflets. Significant disagreement on whether this limitation undermines findings.

Both address C-terminal mCitrine tag concerns (C125-C129). OpenEval supports authors' arguments that flexible linker minimizes steric effects and prior work showed normal interactions. Peer Reviewer 1 explicitly raises concern that mCitrine could disrupt hypothesized NTD-CTD interaction, marking as UNCERTAIN. OpenEval more accepting of authors' counterarguments than peer review.

Both support the authors' discussion of FRET limitations (C137-C142, C152-C157). OpenEval emphasizes the sound logic that FRET bias toward closest approach strengthens the no-binding conclusion. Peer Reviewer 2 acknowledges inherent limitations but accepts the interpretation. Agreement that limitations don't undermine main conclusions.

Related discussions of unroofing limitations (C133-C136). OpenEval (R15) supports authors' acknowledgment of limitations in broader context of experimental constraints. Peer review (R9) more critical, emphasizing that unroofing removes interacting proteins and affects both membrane leaflets. Peer review more concerned about this limitation.

Both address memFRET model uncertainties (C152-C157). OpenEval supports authors' distinction between effects on absolute measurements versus trends. Peer Reviewer 2 acknowledges limitations without challenging interpretation. Agreement that uncertainties in absolute distances don't invalidate trend observations.

OpenEval supports the critical analysis of prior work (C98-C109), particularly identification of YFP pH sensitivity as confounding factor and calculation showing prior FRET efficiencies correspond to implausible distances. No corresponding peer review evaluation explicitly addresses this critique of prior literature.

OpenEval supports the comparison to prior work (C112-C120), noting agreement on NTD topology with Couch et al. and reasonable attribution of CTD differences to methodological/species variations. Peer review mentions consistency with prior work (R3 references C116) but doesn't provide detailed evaluation of this comparative analysis.

OpenEval marks speculation about ASIC1a NTD function (C160-C162) as UNCERTAIN, noting the parallel to P2X receptors is interesting but untested by functional data. No corresponding peer review evaluation addresses this speculative discussion.
